Hi Priya — thanks, and glad the demo landed well. Quick notes and two proposed paths below.

Short answer: we can support a 12-month private offer with monthly billing, but the commercial terms and discount banding change depending on commitment structure and billing cadence. To be explicit:

Option A — 12-month usage-first (monthly billed):
- No upfront prepay; monthly metered billing based on actual tokens.
- Discount band: 5–15% off list depending on monthly run rate.
- Requires standard Marketplace PO plus delegated approver tree on your side.

Option B — 12-month annual commit (invoiced monthly or net-30):
- Customer commits to an ARR target; deeper discount (15–30%) available based on commitment level.
- Redwood escalation: discounts >20% require Sales Manager signoff; >30% needs VP approval.

Operational asks for a smooth private offer:
- Full approver list (name, title, email) for Marketplace buyer delegation (send Manish if easier).
- SOC2 report and any perf SLAs you expect — helps us size support and SLA add-ons.
- If you want co-sell credits, mention pipeline influence and expected close timeline so we can align partner ops.

I attached a private_offer_template.xlsx that outlines fields we push to AWS Marketplace for private offers (term, billing cadence, pricing matrix). Vanessa — can you confirm internal approval lanes and how much flexibility we have on a metered 12-month plan? Ben — finance implications for monthly-billed private offers?

Proposed next step: brief call Tue morning to lock band and approvals; if you can share the approver roster before then, we'll prepare a DocuSign-ready private offer and HubSpot deal.

Thanks —
Vivek
Head of Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference

Vivek / Ben — internal note (do not forward externally):

- For a metered 12-month private offer we can keep discounts in the 5–15% window. Finance flagged that monthly-billed private offers introduce AR churn risk; recommend adding a 90-day minimum usage threshold to avoid immediate churn exploitation.
- Discount approval matrix (summary):
  * Up to 15% — Sales Manager approval (Vanessa)
  * 15%–25% — VP Sales approval
  * >25% — Revenue Ops + CRO approval (rare)

- If Acme wants >20%, we need a signed mutual action plan with milestones (tech onboarding, monthly check-ins) and a co-sell motion justification. That will get us to VP lane faster.

I attached the discount matrix we used for Q1 pilots. Also, if we offer monthly metered billing, Billing needs to add a 90-day rolling minimum before we can auto-suspend for low usage. Ben — can you confirm cashflow exposure if we do net-30 invoices rather than prepay?

Thanks,
Vanessa
Sr. Director, Channel & Marketplace Ops
Redwood Inference
